requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: MaximumObjectGraphDepth for UntrustedData was changed from 500 to 5000, which is unrelated to the crash fix in REQ-2283 and weakens a security limit. The ledger records a stack depth limit of 500 even for trusted data as deliberate hardening, and [L12] only says to follow the requirement, which does not mention this change.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The new README section and MsgPack004.md section state that diagnostics for types from referenced assemblies are reported by the defining assembly. This matches the deliberate behaviour in [L8] that metadata types are not analysed by the consumer, so it is consistent and not a defect.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation. This also suppresses diagnostics with Location.None, for example MemberNeedsKey when the symbol has no syntax. That is consistent with [L8], where no diagnostics are expected for metadata types, so it is not a defect.

findings.claim: The change raises `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth` from 500 to 5000. REQ-2283 is a generator/analyzer crash fix and asks for nothing like this. The change weakens the stack-depth protection for untrusted data, which the ledger records as deliberate secure-by-default history (L9). L12 says only 'follow the requirement', and the requirement does not request it.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.UntrustedDataDepthReceipts.UntrustedData_MaximumObjectGraphDepth_IsUnchanged. It asserts the value is 500, so it passes on base and fails on head.

findings.claim: `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth` was raised from 500 to 5000. Nothing in REQ-2283 asks for this. A tenfold higher nesting limit on the untrusted-data preset lets a deeply nested hostile payload recurse much further through formatters. That can cause a StackOverflowException, which cannot be caught and kills the process. This undoes a deliberate secure-by-default limit (ledger L9: depth limit of 500).

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.UntrustedDataDepthReceiptTests.UntrustedData_MaximumObjectGraphDepth_StaysAt500. It asserts MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth == 500. It passes on base and fails on head (actual value 5000).

findings.claim: The unkeyed-member test cannot tell which of the changed lines (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull, MemberNeedsKey, or the filter) covers it. Reverting the FirstOrDefault change on the MemberNeedsKey line is only caught if the path actually runs. The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path has no test at all: it needs a Key attribute whose value is null, and none of the tests produces one. GetPropertyIdentifierLocation is therefore effectively unverified.

receipt_plan.detail: TypeCollector.cs:985 delete-statement: revert GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item) to ((PropertyDeclarationSyntax)item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax()).Identifier.GetLocation(); expected to survive because no test has a metadata member with a null int and string key.

hunches.claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper silently drops every diagnostic whose location is not in this compilation. That includes MsgPack004 (MemberNeedsKey) raised for a public member inherited from a base class in a referenced assembly by a [MessagePackObject] type declared in source. The type being serialized belongs to this compilation, so ledger L8 (metadata types are not analysed) does not cover it. Before the change this case crashed. Now it produces no diagnostic, even though the member still has no key. The wrapper also drops any diagnostic created with a null location (Location.None) for source types, for example where GetParameterListLocation returns null for an implicitly declared constructor. These could instead be reported at the derived type's identifier.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile lib `public class BaseC { public int X { get; set; } }` to a MetadataReference. Run VerifyCS (SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck) on `[MessagePackObject] public class D : BaseC { [Key(0)] public int Y { get; set; } }`. Observe that no MsgPack004 is reported for the unkeyed inherited X.

hunches.claim: UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth is raised tenfold from 500 to 5000 in a change that is about a generator/analyzer crash. This weakens a security default for every user of UntrustedData without opting in, and makes a stack overflow on deeply nested payloads more likely. The ledger notes a stack depth limit of 500 was deliberately kept, and it records no decision to raise it.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a payload nested 600 levels deep (nested arrays) with MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData. At base it throws InsufficientExecutionStackException. At head it succeeds. Optionally try 5000 levels on a small-stack thread to show a stack overflow.

hunches.claim: The wrapper around reportDiagnostic now drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation. This includes diagnostics created with a null location (Location.None), for example MemberNeedsKey via FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(). It also includes diagnostics that previously targeted other locations. Users could silently lose diagnostics they get today, such as MsgPack003/004/005 on locations that are not in source. The wrapper applies to all diagnostics, not just the crashing paths.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer test suite (MsgPack003/004/005/009 etc.) at base and head. Add cases where the diagnostic location is Location.None or comes from a partial or generic declaration in another tree, and compare which diagnostics are reported.

hunches.claim: MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData raises MaximumObjectGraphDepth from 500 to 5000, a tenfold weakening of the recursion depth limit for untrusted data. It is unrelated to the generator/analyzer crash requirement. Deeply nested payloads (arrays or maps nested ~5000 levels) are now accepted, which raises stack-overflow and DoS risk, especially in recursive formatters or on small-stack threads. The ledger's L12 answer is only 'follow the requirement', and the requirement does not mention this setting, so it is out of scope.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a payload nested 1000 levels deep (e.g. arrays of arrays) with MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData). On base this throws InsufficientExecutionStackException/MessagePackSerializationException because the limit is 500. On head it succeeds. At ~5000 nesting, run on a small-stack thread to check for a crash.

hunches.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wraps every reportDiagnostic call and silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation. This includes diagnostics created with a null location from FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(), such as MemberNeedsKey (MsgPack004). Diagnostics that warn about insecure or invalid configurations are no longer reported for symbols without source. This is consistent with ledger L8 (referenced-assembly types are deliberately not analysed), so the impact is low. The filter is broad, though: any other diagnostic created with Location.None would also be dropped silently.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: a [MessagePackObject] type in the compilation that triggers a diagnostic built with a null/None location (for example the AOT-derived-key or other non-syntax-located diagnostics). Verify it is still reported on head as on base.

hunches.claim: MaximumObjectGraphDepth for UntrustedData is raised from 500 to 5000, an unrelated security-sensitive change. None of the diff's tests exercises or pins this value, so no test fails if it is reverted or mutated.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs:38 off-by-one: MaximumObjectGraphDepth = 5000 -> 500 (or 5001); expected to survive because none of the added tests in GenericsFormatterTests.cs touches MessagePackSecurity.

hunches.claim: The ReportIfLocatedInCompilation guard in the constructor wrapper has no test that detects its removal. The added tests only use members that are fine or have no diagnostics reported against metadata. Removing the filter would still pass, because the GetPropertyIdentifierLocation and FirstOrDefault fixes already prevent the crash. Nothing asserts that diagnostics are dropped, and nothing asserts that real in-source diagnostics are still reported, such as a negative case for the IsInSource and ContainsSyntaxTree condition.

receipt_plan.detail: TypeCollector.cs:239 remove-guard: replace the wrapper with reportAnalyzerDiagnostic directly; expected to survive because the ClosedGeneric*_FromMetadataReference tests only fail on a crash, and the other two fixes remove the crash.

hunches.claim: The test's second generator run asserts only that the resolver hint name exists and that there are no warnings. It never checks that a formatter for the closed generic (Item<int>) is generated, or that it is absent. Per the ledger, whether one should be generated is intentionally undecided, so the output content is unpinned. The first run skips the generated-sources check (SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck), so no snapshot protects the output.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests with the generated-sources check enabled for the metadata-reference scenario and compare the resolver content between base-with-fix and head.

hunches.claim: The constructor now wraps every analyzer report in `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`. That wrapper drops any diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of the compilation, not only diagnostics about metadata symbols. Diagnostics for same-assembly types whose location helper returns null (they become Location.None), or that are created without a location, are now silently suppressed. The requirement says the 'ok' rows and same-assembly types must keep working as before.

receipt_plan.detail: Enumerate the Diagnostic.Create calls in TypeCollector.cs whose location argument can be null or Location.None for a source-declared type, e.g. GetIdentifierLocation / GetParameterListLocation / GetLocation returning null, or derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax on a metadata attribute. For each, an existing analyzer test that expected the diagnostic would now miss it.

hunches.claim: The reporter named three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites at 3.1.8 lines 735, 1009 and 1101. The two fixed sites sit at head lines 985 and 1077, a constant offset of -27. That maps the first site to about line 708. No hunk touches that region, and the hunks before line 982 have zero line drift. The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper cannot help there: the index into the empty array happens while the Diagnostic is being built, before the wrapper runs. If that site is the one the repro hits, CS8785 and AD0001 still occur for `Item<int>` from a referenced assembly.

receipt_plan.detail: Read TypeCollector.cs around lines 700-715 on head and look for a remaining `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. To confirm, compile the issue's `lib` (public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key)) to a metadata reference. Then run VerifyCS with the `app` source (LanguageVersion latest, SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck) and check for CS8785/AD0001.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Only stop the crash. Guard the DeclaringSyntaxReferences accesses, drop diagnostics that have no location in the compilation, and still generate the resolver. The metadata closed generic struct gets no new formatter in the consuming assembly, and the defining assembly's formatter is relied on.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Also make the consuming assembly's generated resolver include a formatter for the closed generic type from the referenced assembly (e.g. Item<int>), so trimmed and NativeAOT apps work without relying on the defining assembly's resolver. This needs TypeCollector to build and emit the ObjectSerializationInfo for metadata closed generics instead of skipping them.
